newsitem.title: GREECE: ING Barings sets new call warrant on Greek banks.
newsitem.headline: ING Barings sets new call warrant on Greek banks.

text.p: ING Baring Financial Products launched new American-style, $-denominated call warrants on a basket of Greek bank shares with Sigma Securities acting as the local placing agent.
The warrants will be listed in Luxembourg and offer investors exposure to the following stock basket:
"The US dollar notional of call warrants are American style with expiry in one year. They are 110 percent out-of-the-money and have an offering price of $14.05 each," ING Barings said.
The warrant premium is also payable in drachmas at no extra charge to the investor. Each warrant controls $100 of the underlying shares and the minimum trading lot is 1000 warrants.

"The issue offers investors several advantages over buying the physical stock including avoiding the costs of custody and settlement arrangements. In a single transaction, investors can gain geared exposure to a selected portfolio of blue-chip banking stocks," it said.

Greece's stock market has appreciated by 46.2 percent in drachma terms and by 37.2 percent in dollar terms year to date. The banking basket has risen 63.3 percent in dollar terms since the beginning of the year.
